title: Break The Spin · Nov 26 (morning picks)
subtitle: 5 posts, real photos. Scott approved. Boston first so it posts today.

posts.quote: Boston City Council Votes To Call Thanksgiving A "Day Of Mourning."
posts.alt: Photo of the public-domain painting The First Thanksgiving, 1621, by J.L.G. Ferris, showing Pilgrims and Wampanoag sharing a meal, with a circle inset of Boston City Hall. Text reads: Boston City Council Votes To Call Thanksgiving A "Day Of Mourning." Break The Spin logo top left. Credits: J.L.G. Ferris (public domain); Daderot, CC0.
posts.caption: Boston's City Council voted to recognize Thanksgiving as a "National Day of Mourning." Third year in a row. The resolution says the Thanksgiving story "sanitizes the English colonists' invasion of Wampanoag homelands." It cancels nothing. Twelve of 13 councilors signed on.
posts.first: The facts: Resolution 2026-2174, sponsored by Councilor Benjamin Weber, passed Nov. 18. It is symbolic only. Similar resolutions passed in 2024 (13-0) and 2025. Sources: Boston City Council dockets 2026-2174 and 2024-1723; City of Boston council newsletter (2025).

posts.theme: ICE Boston arrests $1 million lottery winner
posts.quote: Illegal Immigrant Won $1 Million In The Lottery. ICE Arrested Him On A 12-Year-Old Deportation Order.
posts.alt: Photo of an ICE officer in tactical gear, back to the camera, with POLICE on the vest and red emergency lights at left, and a circle inset of an ICE Special Response Team patch. Text reads: Illegal Immigrant Won $1 Million In The Lottery. ICE Arrested Him On A 12-Year-Old Deportation Order. Break The Spin logo top left. Photo credit: ICE / DHS. This is a 2025 ICE ERO Boston operation photo, not the lottery-winner arrest.
posts.caption:
He won $1 million on a $10 scratch ticket.

Ariel Velasquez-Morales bought it at a market in East Boston. The game was the Massachusetts Lottery's "$2,000,000 50X Cashword." He took the cash option: $650,000 before taxes. He posed with the giant check. He told the lottery he planned to save and invest it.

Then ICE Boston showed up.

They arrested him Nov. 24. He will stay in custody pending removal from the United States.

Here's why. He crossed the border illegally in 2013, during the Obama administration. Border Patrol in Texas' Rio Grande Valley issued him a notice to appear in immigration court and released him into the country, with a list of free legal service providers. A Department of Justice immigration judge ordered him removed in 2014. He stayed anyway. For 12 years.

"Looks like his luck ran out," said ICE Assistant Director of Public Affairs Micah Bock.

ICE Boston was blunter on X: "Welcome to the ERO Boston lottery! Where illegal aliens and sanctuary politicians are out of luck, and the law-abiding citizens of New England are always the winners!"

ICE did not allege a criminal offense beyond the immigration violation. He ignored a judge's removal order and remained in the country. That was enough.

And no, you do not have to be a citizen to buy a Massachusetts lottery ticket. You have to be 18. To claim a prize over $601, you show photo ID and a Social Security number. He claimed the prize. Days later, ICE arrested him.

A removal order is not a suggestion. Twelve years later, ICE cashed the ticket.
posts.first:
The facts: ICE Boston arrested Ariel Velasquez-Morales, a Salvadoran national, on Nov. 24, 2026, after he won a $1 million prize in the Massachusetts Lottery and took a $650,000 lump sum before taxes. ICE said he entered illegally in 2013 and that an immigration judge ordered him removed in 2014. NBC Boston, citing ICE, reported the entry date as May 15, 2013, and the removal order as April 24, 2014. The $10 price is the official cost of the Lottery's "$2,000,000 50X Cashword" game, confirmed by the Massachusetts State Lottery via local reporting. ICE's own release attributed the $10 figure to local reporting. ICE did not allege a separate criminal charge. How ICE identified him was not confirmed; the lottery said winners must present photo ID and a Social Security number to claim prizes over $601.

Sources: ICE press release (Nov. 25), NBC Boston, Boston Globe, Boston.com, Patch (Massachusetts State Lottery prize details).

posts.theme: Pritzker opts Illinois out of federal scholarship tax credit
posts.quote: Pritzker Says No To Trump's School Scholarships. Illinois Kids Lose Out.
posts.alt: Official portrait photo of Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker in a dark suit against a blue backdrop, with a circle inset of President Donald Trump's official 2025 portrait. Text reads: Pritzker Says No To Trump's School Scholarships. Illinois Kids Lose Out. Break The Spin logo top left. Photo credits: Official portraits, State of Illinois / DoD; The White House.
posts.caption:
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker blocked a federal scholarship his own residents can still pay for.

On Nov. 24 he announced that Illinois will not opt into the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, the school-choice program in President Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill. Starting Jan. 1, 2027, a taxpayer can donate up to $1,700, or $3,400 for a married couple, to an authorized scholarship group and get a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit. The scholarships can pay for private or public school costs, tutoring, special education, books and supplies. Families making up to three times their area's median income would have qualified.

Pritzker said no. So Illinois children cannot receive those scholarships.

Here is the part that matters. Illinois taxpayers can still claim the credit. They have to donate to scholarship groups in states that opted in. The money can leave Illinois. Illinois kids get nothing.

"We should not siphon money from public schools for private education," Pritzker said. That is the spin. This credit does not pull a dollar out of an Illinois school budget. It is a federal tax credit for voluntary donations. Public-school students can use the scholarships too.

Teachers unions celebrated. "Public dollars belong in public schools," said Illinois Federation of Teachers and Chicago Teachers Union President Stacy Davis Gates.

Other Democratic governors did not follow his lead. New York's Kathy Hochul and Colorado's Jared Polis opted in. At least 30 states have joined the program.

Teach Coalition CEO Sydney Altfield told Fox News the opt-out could send "over about $2 billion in estimated scholarship money" out of state. That is an advocacy group's estimate, not an official score. The mechanism is not in dispute. Illinois families lose the scholarships. Illinois donors can still take the credit. The money can walk over the border.

Pritzker said he was protecting public schools. He opted Illinois children out of the help, and left the door open for the money to go somewhere else.
posts.first:
The facts: Pritzker announced the opt-out on Nov. 24, 2026. The Federal Scholarship Tax Credit takes effect Jan. 1, 2027. It is a nonrefundable dollar-for-dollar federal credit for donations of up to $1,700 a year, or $3,400 for a married couple, to authorized scholarship-granting organizations. Scholarships may be used for private, public, and charter school expenses, including tutoring and books, and are limited to families earning up to 300% of area median income. Illinois taxpayers can still claim the credit by donating to groups in participating states. The "$2 billion" figure is Teach Coalition CEO Sydney Altfield's estimate, given to Fox News; a separate Democrats for Education Reform analysis cited by Illinois Policy projected about $2.09 billion if 30% of eligible Illinois taxpayers donated the maximum. Neither is an official government score.

Sources: Chalkbeat, WTTW, Capitol News Illinois, ABC7 Chicago, Fox News, Illinois Policy.

posts.quote: Biden's New Book Says Watergate Made Him Run For Senate. He Announced Before Watergate Happened.
posts.alt: Official portrait photo of President Joe Biden, with a circle inset of President Richard Nixon's official portrait. Text reads: Biden's New Book Says Watergate Made Him Run For Senate. He Announced Before Watergate Happened. Break The Spin logo top left. Photo credits: Official portraits, The White House.
posts.caption: In his memoir, "Promise Me, America," Biden writes, "One of the reasons I first ran for the Senate in 1972 was that I was angered by a growing pattern of lies coming out of Washington." He declared in January 1972. The Watergate break-in was June 17, 1972.
posts.first: The facts: Chapter 2 quote reported by the Washington Free Beacon. Roll Call reported he declared in January 1972. Sources: Washington Free Beacon (Nov. 25), Roll Call (2019), U.S. Senate Historical Office.

posts.theme: Gillibrand letter on Amtrak firearms policy
posts.quote: 20 Senators Fight Amtrak's Plan To Let Passengers Bring Locked, Unloaded Guns.
posts.alt: Official portrait photo of Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, with a circle inset of an Amtrak Acela train on the tracks. Text reads: 20 Senators Fight Amtrak's Plan To Let Passengers Bring Locked, Unloaded Guns. Break The Spin logo top left. Photo credits: U.S. Senate; 4300streetcar, CC BY 4.0.
posts.caption:
Amtrak plans to let passengers bring unloaded guns onto trains in locked cases, including in passenger cars on routes with no checked baggage. The change starts in January 2027. Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand led 19 colleagues in a Nov. 19 letter telling Amtrak to drop it.

The firearm would have to be unloaded, in a hard case with two locks, one from the passenger and one from Amtrak, with six hours' notice at a staffed station. That is a locked, unloaded firearm in carry-on baggage, inside the passenger car.

They wrote that they are "alarmed" and that the plan "would not meet the standards established by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) for air travel." They want answers by Dec. 9.

Amtrak has allowed unloaded, locked guns in checked baggage on some routes since 2009. The new part is the passenger car, on busy routes such as the Northeast Regional. The letter was signed by 19 Democrats and Independent Sen. Angus King of Maine. The senators are treating a locked case like an open-carry problem.
posts.first: The facts: The Nov. 19 letter to Interim Amtrak President Byl Herrmann was led by Sen. Gillibrand and signed by 19 other senators, including Sen. Angus King (I-Maine). It asks Amtrak to reconsider the January 2027 carry-on policy and wants answers by Dec. 9. Amtrak has allowed unloaded firearms in checked baggage on some routes since 2009. Sources: Gillibrand press release and letter (Nov. 19).
